subject: reject singular cov_matrix or let through?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: reject singular cov_matrix or let through?
parts:
We're way off topic on ragged arrays, I think, so
I started a new thread on stan-dev and off the issue.

Ben's example is:

> cov_matrix[2] Sigma;
> Sigma[1,1] <- 1;
> Sigma[1,2] <- 1 - 1e-17;
> Sigma[2,1] <- Sigma[1,2]
> Sigma[2,2] <- 1;

We know that

(1 - 1e-17) == 1

and thus Sigma == [[1 1] [1 1]] will be singular.

The question I have is whether we should be

1. allow this through, or

2. throw an exception so that NUTS and throw away the
branch of the binary tree it's working on and sets n_divergent
to 1 for that iteration.

If (1) is the desired behavior, that can be achieved
now by declaring Sigma as matrix[2,2] rather than cov_matrix[2].

- Bob

> On Mar 26, 2015, at 3:59 PM, bgoodri <notifi...@github.com> wrote:
>
> Well, it is that multiply_lower_tri_self_transpose produces numerically
> unstable results. Even though it maximizes the precision, it can't preserve
> enough precision for a Cholesky factorization to come out with positive
> diagonals. Just
>
> cov_matrix[2] Sigma;
> Sigma[1,1] <- 1;
> Sigma[1,2] <- 1 - 1e-17;
> Sigma[2,1] <- Sigma[1,2]
> Sigma[2,2] <- 1;
>
> will underflow the off-diagonal element and result in a numerically
> singular matrix.
>
> On Thu, Mar 26, 2015 at 12:45 AM, Daniel Lee <notifi...@github.com>
> wrote:

> > I've managed to get an example running and I see it's failing, but is that

On Thursday, March 26, 2015 at 7:54:29 AM UTC-4, Bob Carpenter wrote:
The question I have is whether we should be

1. allow this through, or

2. throw an exception so that NUTS and throw away the
branch of the binary tree it's working on and sets n_divergent
to 1 for that iteration.

or

3. Stop sampling entirely.

And the right answer to that question can't be determined from the numbers in the matrix. So, you have to make some assumption about the code that generated it.

Ben
